$comment: Sites whose PAINT VALUE is runtime data. A skin rule cannot hold them, and emitting one custom
property per swatch or datum would be strictly worse code than the inline value. They are NOT
pending work: carrying them as debt that can never reach 0 is a lie in the ratchet, and it sends
migration agents chasing an impossible zero.
Each entry declares a FLOOR: the number of sites that must REMAIN inline in that file. The gate
enforces it in both directions -- a file may not drop below its floor (someone migrated paint
that cannot live in CSS), and the floor is what a migration's exit criterion is measured against
Counts come from the WO-SKIN-06 inventories (ck-e, ck-h, ck-f). Update them ONLY with a measured
recount, never to make a gate go green.

SKIN-EXEMPT-RUNTIME-VALUE.$why: The paint value is data supplied at runtime: a tenant's chosen brand hex, a per-datum chart colour, a per-user identity colour. Three of the four components here exist specifically to SHOW THE USER A COLOUR THEY PICKED.

patterns/misc/tenant-preview/engines/mod.why: buildPaletteSteps() mixes a 10-step palette from the tenant's chosen hex (mixColor(base, '#fff'|'#000', ratio)), then renders it as swatches, buttons and badges.

patterns/misc/tenant-preview/engines/rus.why: The same 10 palette steps, plus 4 render sites. NOTE: rustic's Button/Input/Badge sections use generic DS scale tokens instead of the tenant's actual colour -- a real cross-engine inconsistency, filed separately, not something the migration may 'fix'.

patterns/misc/brand-studio/index.tsx.why: index.tsx:387 -- background: isHex(value) ? value : 'transparent', the live swatch of the field the admin is typing into.

patterns/communication/presence/index.ts.why: Per-user identity colours (ringColor/cursorColor) that stay inline: the avatar ring border, the avatar-initials colour, and the LiveCursor name-badge background -- 3 COUNTER-VISIBLE runtime object-literal sites. A 4th true-runtime site (the LiveCursor SVG `fill={cursorColor}` presentation attribute) is also inline but is INVISIBLE to the inline-paint counter (it is a JSX attribute, not a style-object key), so the counter's floor is 3, not the 4-site true-runtime total the CK-F inventory recorded. Recalibrated to the counter's measurement basis after the CK-F migration verified all runtime sites correctly inline at counter=3.

patterns/visualization/charts/bar-chart/.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: single-series `d.color ?? palette[i % palette.length]` and multi-series `s.color ?? palette[i % palette.length]` -- the actual bar fill itself is D3-imperative (`.attr('fill', ...)`), invisible to this counter; only the legend re-consumption of the same per-datum/per-series value is census-visible.

patterns/visualization/charts/line-chart.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `s.color ?? palette[i % palette.length]` (1), plus the same per-series color re-consumed a second time as `color` inside the `items={rows.map(...)}` array literal fed to `<TooltipSeries>` on hover (1). The line stroke/area-gradient/dot fill itself is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/area-chart.why: Same shape as line-chart: legend swatch backgroundColor (1) + tooltip `items[].color` re-consumption (1). The area fill/gradient itself is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/radar-char.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `s.color ?? palette[i % palette.length]` (1), plus `palette[0]` used twice as the default series color (`[{ name: 'Data', data, color: palette[0] }]`) when no `series` prop is passed -- two separate source occurrences, both real value-object literals, not a type annotation.

patterns/visualization/charts/scatter/in.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `d.color ?? colors[i % colors.length]`. Point fill/stroke is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/pie-chart/.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `d.color ?? palette[i % palette.length]`. Slice fill is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/treemap/in.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `palette[i % palette.length]` -- no per-item override at all, pure index cycling, still B because `palette`/`colors` itself is a caller-supplied array. Tile fill is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/funnel-cha.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `d.color ?? colors[i % colors.length]`. Segment fill is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/waterfall/.why: The 3 legend-array `color:` entries (`increaseColor`/`decreaseColor`/`totalColor`, each typed `?: string` with a static-token default) plus their re-consumption as `item.color` on the swatch backgroundColor (1) -- 4 sites total, all traceable to the same 3 caller-overridable props. Bar fill is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/histogram/.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor for `color` (bar fill prop, default var(--ds-color-primary)) and `cumulativeColor` (line/dot prop, default var(--ds-color-info)) -- both typed `?: string` with a static-token default, arbitrary once overridden. Bar/line/dot painting itself is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/gauge/inde.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `seg.color` from the caller-suppliable `segments` array (DEFAULT_SEGMENTS' own 3 literal color values are A-static -- they are hardcoded fallback defaults, not a runtime read). `needleColor` (typed `?: string`, default var(--ds-color-text-primary)) feeds 3 D3 `.attr()` calls and is real B, but is NEVER a census-visible object-literal site anywhere in this file -- it cannot be floor-protected by this counter-based gate at all, same class as `crosshair.ts`'s dot fill (see the family $excluded note).

patterns/visualization/charts/bullet/ind.why: `resolvedRangeColors[0..2]`/`valueColor`/`targetColor` (5, built into the legend array) + `item.color` re-consumption on the swatch backgroundColor (1) + the `rangeBands` array literal (`{ upper, color: resolvedRangeColors[n] }`) rebuilt independently in BOTH the horizontal (3) and vertical (3) orientation branches. All 12 trace back to the same caller-overridable `rangeColors`/`valueColor`/`targetColor` props; the value-bar/target-marker/range-band fills themselves are D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/sankey/ind.why: Node layout object `color: n.color ?? colors[i % colors.length]` (1), link layout object `color: link.color ?? sn.color` -- a second-order fallback through the link's SOURCE NODE's already-resolved color, not independently computable (1), plus the node legend swatch backgroundColor re-consumption (1). Node/link fill itself is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/network-gr.why: Legend swatch backgroundColor: `colors[i % colors.length]`. Node fill (`groupColor()` or `d.color`) is D3-imperative, invisible here.

patterns/visualization/charts/tooltip/in.why: `TooltipValue`'s and `TooltipSeries`'s swatch `backgroundColor: color`/`backgroundColor: item.color` -- both a caller-supplied per-series/per-value color passed into the shared tooltip components every chart in the family mounts. The other 9 sites in this file (TOOLTIP_STYLE ×5, SWATCH_STYLE ×1, label colors ×3) are all static tokens.

patterns/visualization/kanban-board/engi.why: Column header `borderTop: column.color ? \`3px solid ${column.color}\` : undefined` -- per-column caller-supplied accent color, no enum.
Same shape as modern: column header `borderTop`, keyed on the caller-supplied `column.color`.

patterns/visualization/calendar-view/eng.why: Event chip `background: ev.color ?? 'var(--ds-color-primary)'` -- per-event caller-supplied color.
Same shape as modern: event chip `background`, keyed on the caller-supplied `ev.color`.

patterns/visualization/map-view/engines/.why: Marker color dot `background: marker.color`, conditionally rendered only when `marker.color` is present -- per-marker caller-supplied color with NO fallback token at all (pre-existing gap, not migration-caused; every other per-item color in this checkpoint has a `?? var(--ds-*)` default, this one does not).
Same shape as modern: marker color dot `background: marker.color`, same no-fallback gap.

patterns/forms/form-builder/engines/mode.why: form-builder/engines/modern.tsx:282 -- the color field's read-only swatch paints `background: String(val)`, the hex the USER PICKED in that field. A value computed from data; no token set can hold it. No rustic twin (rustic renders no swatch).

SKIN-EXEMPT-RUNTIME-VALUE.$excluded: charts/hooks/use-chart-theme.ts:291 is DEAD CODE (the hook has no callers anywhere in the repo, verified by grep). Do NOT exempt it -- exempting dead code freezes it in place with the gate's blessing. Wire it up or delete it; either way that is a product decision, not an exemption. charts/tooltip/crosshair.ts's dot-fill B site (`.attr('fill', (d) => d.color)`) is also real B but is 100% D3-imperative -- the file's own census count is 0, so it is invisible to this counter-based gate and cannot be floor-protected here at all; same for gauge/index.tsx's `needleColor` (see that file's own why).

SKIN-EXEMPT-CRASH-SAFE-FALLBACK.$why: Paint that must render when the theming provider itself has crashed. It cannot depend on a token, a skin, or anything the failure might have taken down.

surfaces/foundation/SurfaceErrorBoundary.why: Hardcoded hex values, deliberately. The component's own comment says it must render even when the theme provider crashes -- a token would resolve to nothing in exactly the situation this component exists for.

SKIN-EXEMPT-NOT-PAINT.$why: Paint-shaped property names on objects that never reach a DOM style prop. Not A, not B: migrating them is a category error -- no CSS selector can hold a TypeScript mutation.

patterns/misc/brand-studio/index.tsx.why: BrandTheme DRAFT mutations (ctl.buttonPrimary = { ..., color: v }) and a hostile-theme test fixture. The admin's keystroke is written into a theme object, not painted. Lines 229, 323, 328, 763, 765, 767, 769, 775.
patterns/misc/brand-studio/index.tsx.$note: This file appears in two exemption families; its total floor is the SUM (1 runtime-value + 8 not-paint = 9).
